component.name: Apache NuttX
component.description: Real-time operating system designed for portability across more than 15 CPU architectures and minimal-footprint devices. The published security page combines a short statement of what is and is not considered a security vulnerability, the project's vulnerability handling process (reporting, investigation, resolution, and public announcement phases following Apache Security Team guidelines), and the list of published CVEs.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

threats.name: Missing input validation in custom application or firmware code
threats.description: Because NuttX prioritizes portability and a minimal footprint, validation of function parameters and incoming data rests on the custom application/firmware developer and is not considered a NuttX security vulnerability. Areas requiring developer caution include system calls, pointer handling (initialization and cleanup), structure initialization patterns, validation of user-controllable data types and sizes, network data processing, and dynamic buffer management.

threats.name: Generic codebase issues affecting confidentiality, integrity, or availability
threats.description: Issues in the generic NuttX codebase that affect confidentiality, integrity, or availability are treated as security vulnerabilities. They should be reported privately to the security team (security@nuttx.apache.org, copied to security@apache.org) rather than through public bug trackers, issues, or pull requests, and are handled through the project's reporting, investigation, resolution, and public announcement phases with CVE assignment.

controls.name: Application and firmware developers validate their inputs
controls.description: Custom application and firmware developers must validate function parameters and incoming data, taking care with system calls, pointer initialization and cleanup, structure initialization, user-controllable data type and size validation, network data processing, and dynamic buffer management.

controls.name: Coordinated private vulnerability handling
controls.description: Reports go to security@nuttx.apache.org in plain text, one vulnerability per email, with no public disclosure until the announcement. The team investigates under confidentiality, agrees a fix privately, requests a CVE via Apache's internal portal, commits fixes without security-related references, cuts a release with the patch, and only then announces publicly (release channels, the reporter, project security lists, and oss-security).
